Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's it from the coverage of this game. The two side will meet again for the second ODI on 20th March. The first ball will be at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT), but as you all know, you can join us early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Tamim Iqbal, the victorious skipper is in for a chat. He says the way they batted was exceptional as the surface had something for the bowlers early on. He adds that Shakib Al Hasan was brilliant and also special recognization to Mushfiqur Rahim as he came in and went on a counter from ball 1 which is not easy. He also adds that the first 20-25 overs, the surface was on a slower side and this is why the batting needs to be applauded. Credits Mushfiqur Rahim for his work behind the sticks and informs that the team has complete faith in him. On his bowling unit he says Taskin Ahmed is a world class bowler and Ebadot Hossain is not far from being one.

Towhid Hridoy wins the Man of the Match award for his exception outing with the bat on debut. He starts by thanking the almighty. Informs that he is hurt a bit as he could not get a ton on his debut but then he is extremely happy about his innings. Mentions that Mushfiqur Rahim helped him a lot in the middle to remain calm. Adds that he just tried to execute his plans and that worked wonderfully for him.

Andy Balbirnie, the skipper of Ireland is in for a chat. He starts by saying that at the half-way stage they felt that this was a total they could chase and also the wicket was better but the batters failed to click after the opening stand was broken. He also adds that the team was a bit of unaware about the surroundings but no excuses and hopes that they will be way better in the next game. He closes by saying that they want to compete and beat teams like Bangladesh on a regular basis.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Earlier in the innings, Bangladesh kept losing early wickets. They were three down inside the Powerplay 1, but Shakib Al Hasan and Towhid Hridoy took the game to the opposition. Both the batters though slipped out in their 90s. Mushfiqur Rahim's cameo of 44 runs down the order really cause a lot of harm to this Ireland side. Later, the lower-middle order contributed a little bit to record Bangladesh's highest ever score in ODI cricket. Eventually, it was a bit too much for Ireland.

Bangladesh bowlers were on fire from the word go. The Ireland openers were able to deal the seamers quite easily with the new ball in hand, to change the trajectory of the match, Tamim Iqbal decided to bring the Nasum Ahmed very early in the Powerplay 1. Still, the Irish batters were scoring runs comfortably. But once, Shakib Al Hasan and Nasum Ahmed started working in tandem, the run flow was certainly halted. Shakib Al Hasan drew the first blood and that opened the floodgates, which Bangladesh capitalized on. It was the seam bowlers who benefitted the most, as Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain combined for 6 wickets, off which four belonged to the latter. Nasum Ahmed picked up three wickets, when he took care of the tail-enders. Also, all of this couldn't have been possible without Mushfiqur Rahim behind the sticks. The veteran was a vital asset, as he held on to 5 catches in the entire innings. Overall, it was a complete bowling performance from the Bangladesh unit.

Chasing 339 that too in Bangladesh is always going to be a tough ask, nonetheless, Ireland got off to a promising start.The runs were not coming in quickly early on, but it was all about assessing the conditions. Paul and Stephen did just that and they put their feet on the gas at the back end of Powerplay 1. The openers set a solid platform up top with a 60-run opening stand, although it went downhill ever since this stand was broken. Ireland lost the remaining 9 wickets for just 95 runs. This is a big concern for Ireland. They surely need their middle-order batters to step up in the next encounter. It was only George Dockrell who tried to force an issue here with his knock of 45 runs.

What a dominating performance from the hosts. Bangladesh have take an early lead in this ODI and that too quite convincingly. Ireland will head back to the drawing board and try to come back stronger in the next outing.

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Fuller delivery in the line of stumps, George Dockrell looks to clear his front leg and loft this over mid off but misses out on this and the ball has crashed into the stumps. It is all over as Bangladesh has won this by a margin of 183 runs.
Slower one, full and on off. George Dockrell gets under it and skies it towards long off. The fielder from mid off gives it a chase but it lands safely.
A length ball, around off, that comes back in. Hume gets it to square leg off the inside edge. One taken. For a second, Ebadot Hossain thought he has his four-fer here.
Full toss, on off. Hume pushes it to point.
A wide yorker, outside off. Hume looks to dig it out but fails to do so.

FOUR! Fuller one on off, George Dockrell smashes this uppishly to long off for a boundary. Litton Das does well to get a hand on this but fails to collect this and the ball has travelled past the boundary.
Fuller outside off, Graham Hume pushes this to backward point for a single.
Fuller one around middle, George Dockrell pushes this to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short in length outside off, George Dockrell smashes this to the fielder at cover.

Tossed up on off, George Dockrell smashes this down the ground for a single to long on.
Graham Hume is the final man in.

OUT! Short-pitched delivery, too quick for Mark Adair as he gets late in his attempt to pull this and gets a faint edge that travels to the keeper and Mushfiqur Rahim makes no mistake and takes it clean.

Fuller one in middle, Mark Adair pushes this to long on for a single.
Short in length around middle, George Dockrell pushes this to long off for a single.

Tossed up in middle, Mark Adair defends this to cover-point for no run.
Fuller one around off, Mark Adair drives this to short cover.
FOUR! Short-pitched delivery head high, George Dockrell pulls this to deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short and wide of off, Mark Adair edges this one bounce past the slip fielder for a single.
Back of a length around off, George Dockrell pushes this to third man for a single.

Fuller one around pads, George Dockrell pushes this to short mid-wicket for no run.

Wide! Good length delivery but down leg, George Dockrell looks to flick but decides to leave this in the end. Wide signaled.
Back of a length outside off, Gareth Delany guides this to third man for a single.

On a length outside off, Gareth Delany blocks this out on the off side.
On a length outside off, Gareth Delany looks to cut but misses out and the keeper collects this.
Fuller around middle, George Dockrell gets a leading edge that flies past the bowler for a single.

Tossed up outside off, George Dockrell pushes this to long off for a single.

Short and wide of off, George Dockrell has lofted this over the fielder at point for a couple.
On a length around the waist, George Dockrell tucks this to short mid-wicket.
Back of a length outside off, George Dockrell pushes this to short cover.
Fuller around middle, George Dockrell flicks this to deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Short in length around middle, George Dockrell cuts this to point for a single.
Fuller one outside off, Curtis Campher drives this to long off for a single.
Tossed up around off, George Dockrell pushes this in the gap on the off side for a single.

Tossed up outside off, George Dockrell defends this in front of him.
Fuller one on pads, Curtis Campher scoops this behind the keeper for 3 runs. The fielder does well to stop 1 run for his team.
Back of a length angling away from stumps, George Dockrell shuts stop and let the keeper collect this without poking at this.

Fuller one around pads, George Dockrell looks to flick but fails to connect and the ball deflects off his pads for no run.

FOUR! George Dockrell breaks the shackles. It is a full-length ball, outside off. George Dockrell carves it through the gap at covers. The ball has enough legs to reach the fence here.
Good length, wide of off. It flies off the deck. George Dockrell throws the kitchen sink on it but fails to get any bat on ball. Four dots in a row.
Short ball, wide of off. George Dockrell leaves it alone.
Full, outside off. George Dockrell blocks it out to the off side.
Swing and a miss! Ahmed dishes a length ball, outside off. George Dockrell now tries to get into the action with a wild slash but only connects with thin air.

Shouts of catch! Lands safely though. It is a length ball, on off. It extracts some extra bounce. Curtis Campher is unable to heave it across the line. The ball takes the outside edge and lobs towards point.
A length ball, on off. Curtis Campher blocks it out watchfully.
Good length, on off, hurries on to the batter. George Dockrell opens the face late and guides it to backward point. A wicket-maiden for Taskin Ahmed this time.
It is pitched up once again, on fourth stump. Andy Balbirnie drives it through the line towards mid off. Hits it nicely but only to meet the fielder.
Full length, on off. George Dockrell dabs it out to point.
A sharp bumper, on off. George Dockrell ducks under this one.
Shorter, on off. George Dockrell blocks it out solidly.
George Dockrell walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT AT SLIPS! Another man bites the dust. Taskin Ahmed gets his second in no time here. It is a length ball, angled in around off. Lorcan Tucker gets a thick outside edge on it. The ball flies towards first slip. It is travelling at a good height. Yasir Ali there at first slip, times his jump to perfection and takes a solid catch with both hands over his head. The required run rate is around 8 runs now.
Commentary.Howout: c Yasir Ali b Taskin Ahmed

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, that lands outside off and nips back in sharply. Curtis Campher hangs back and blocks it under his eyes. A probing over from Ebadot Hossain comes to an end.
Full length, on off. Lorcan Tucker pushes it out for another single.
Length ball, angled in on off. Curtis Campher pushes it gently towards point and gets to the other end.

Is that dropped? No it isn't. It is a short ball, outside off. Curtis Campher cuts it late towards backward point. It meets Towhid Hridoy on a bounce. Although, the bounce is an awkward one and catches the finger of Hridoy. He seems to be in some pain here. The physio is out to have a look. The magic spray comes on and Hridoy is good to continue.
Shortish, around off. Lorcan Tucker dabs it to point and gets a single.
Short one, on off. Lorcan Tucker goes for the pull shot but it comes off the inner half.

JAFFA! Taskin Ahmed asking the right questions here. It is a length ball, in the channel, just shapes away a touch. Curtis Campher hangs his blade away from his body in an attempt to defend it away but instead gets beaten on the outside edge.
Taskin Ahmed hurls in a length ball, on off, angling back in. Curtis Campher gets his blade down in time.
Back of a length, in the channel. Curtis Campher is happy with just a sighter here. He lets it be.

Time for Drinks. Bangladesh is right on top at this point scalping 4 wickets with just 73 on board. The opening pair did show some fight but ever since the first wicket, the wickets have fallen in a cluster. Ireland needs a solid and big partnership if they want to win this game.

OUT! TIMBER! The crowd is on its feet here. Tamim Iqbal is bang on with his bowling change once again. Taskin Ahmed fires in an inswinging yorker, right on the money, on off. Andy Balbirnie stays back and tries to flick it away to the leg side but ends up playing all around it. The ball sneaks through and hits the middle of middle stump. Andy Balbirnie shakes his head and walks off the field here. Ireland are in a spot of bother here.
A length ball, around off. Andy Balbirnie dabs it out to point.
Full length, on middle. Andy Balbirnie shuffles and tucks it towards mid on.
Fuller, angled into the pads. Lorcan Tucker flicks it through mid-wicket for two runs. Another successful over from Ebadot Hossain comes to an end.
BEATEN! It is a length ball, outside off, it shapes away a touch, at 144 clicks. Lorcan Tucker tries to play at it tentatively and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Length and on off. Lorcan Tucker defends it out solidly.
It is a full-length ball, on off. Lorcan Tucker drives it towards extra covers. Tamim Iqbal there misfields. The batters are able to take a couple of runs here.
WIDE! Ebadot Hossain spills it down the leg side. Lorcan Tucker fails to tuck it away. Wide called.
Lorcan Tucker walks out next.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Mushfiqur Rahim has his third catch of the game and a third wicket for Bangladesh as well. Ebadot Hossain has turned the game on its head. Ireland are on the back foot here. It is a full-length ball, on fifth stump. Harry Tector goes for an expansive drive but only manages to get a thick edge on it. Mushfiqur Rahim takes a sharp low catch this time.

Floated and full, attacking the stumps. Harry Tector blocks it out watchfully.
This is pushed through quicker, full and on leg. Andy Balbirnie slogs it towards deep square leg. It is aerial but only briefly. One taken.
On off, defended back to the bowler.

Fuller, around leg. Andy Balbirnie tucks it into mid-wicket for one.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Ebadot Hossain now gets rid of the other opener. Mushfiqur Rahim is old? Well, then I am convinced that age is just a number because Rahim has taken a spectacular catch. Ebadot Hossain digs in a short ball, on middle, it hurries on to the batter. Paul Stirling shuffles inside the crease and tries to pull it away. Paul Stirling though is cramped for room here. He gloves it behind, to the left of the keeper. Rahim flies to his left and takes a stunning catch.

Commentary.Commentary: Ebadot Hossain pitches it up, outside off. Andy Balbirnie leans in and carves it through covers. They only get a single this time.

Full and straight, in line with the stumps. Andy Balbirnie blocks it solidly.
Around off, defended into covers.
Full and on off. Andy Balbirnie helps it back to the bowler.
